subtype: Writing one lesson and one change [Response]
passage:
"So what's the lesson, Ramesh?" Bhupen asked, marker in hand.
"We should have tested with real data."
"True. But that's a wish. What's the concrete change?"
"Add a step to the release checklist: run the sample with last month's real file."
"Who adds it, and by when?"
"I will. Today."
Bhupen wrote on the board: Lesson: test with real data. Change: checklist item, Ramesh, today.
"And next time we look at it at the halfway point, not the end."
"Also written." Ramesh smiled. "It feels better than just saying sorry."
"Regret without a change is only regret," Bhupen said. "Let's see the checklist on Friday."

qa.q: What concrete change did Ramesh propose?
qa.a: Ramesh proposed adding a checklist step to run the sample with last month's real file.

qa.q: How does Ramesh feel by the end of the review?
qa.a: Better and relieved, since a concrete change feels better than just saying sorry.

qa.q: Why did Bhupen push past "test with real data" to a concrete change?
qa.a: A lesson without a changed action is only regret, while a named item, owner and day makes it real.
Bhupen sees it as needing a changed action, not only regret.

grounding: Shows a review that ends with one lesson and one concrete change with an owner and a date.

subtype: Writing one lesson and one change [Response]
passage: Looking back at our failed product demo three years ago, the review was not the hard part. Ending it was. Madhav, my teammate, asked, "What is the one lesson, and what will you do differently on Monday?" I wrote: lesson, I never tested the demo on the venue's network. Change: add "test on the venue network the day before" to my checklist and phone the venue a week earlier. I taped the checklist to my monitor. Every demo since has had that line, and twice it caught a problem. Before that, my reviews were long sighs and no changes. - Amandeep

qa.q: What did Amandeep add to the checklist?
qa.a: Amandeep added "test on the venue network the day before".

qa.q: What did Amandeep realise about the earlier reviews?
qa.a: That they were long sighs and regret without any change.

qa.q: Why did the checklist item work?
qa.a: It turned the lesson into a concrete action, and twice it caught a problem.

qa.q: What did Madhav's question ask Amandeep to do?
qa.a: To name one lesson and one action for Monday, moving from regret to a concrete change.

grounding: Shows a reflective person ending a review with one lesson and one concrete change, such as a checklist item.
